ADR-002 (deterministic delivery status rendering, settled 2026-09-25) decided that delivery status answers are always rendered as a deterministic card with `suppressAssistantResponse: true`. The model never phrases a delivery time, ETA or status in prose. A reviewer on PR #261 (comment 4098626654) proposed dropping the card and letting the model answer in free text, because a rigid card limits the model's flexibility. That was rejected for these reasons:

1. Hallucination and compliance risk. The EU AI Act data-flow record and the `docs/danish-review.md` rows promise that the customer reads delivery status verbatim from the TMS. A paraphrased ETA is the one hallucination the pilot cannot afford.
2. KPIs need cards. The card-rate KPI (SC-006, at least 90% by 2026-Q4) has no denominator if an answer can be prose. The thumbs-up KPI (SC-007, at least 80%) also depends on the card, because ratings attach to card turns and a prose answer produces no rating.
3. The FR-043 amendment. FR-043 of support-agent-tms-tools is being amended to permit a deterministic-render tool. That amendment is the only exception to the prohibition on `suppressAssistantResponse` and `clientMessages`, and without the card it has no justification.
4. The not-found case. It is a deterministic card too, because the model must not invent a shipment it did not fetch. Doing that in prose would be a GDPR-adjacent data-integrity risk.

The exact card UI design in bowman-ui is still open. One open question is how a long set of shipment cards should present, for example an order with twenty shipments, since FR-102 renders every shipment.
